newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Santos has no plans for sympathy strike.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Santos has no plans for sympathy strike.

text.p: Workers at Brazil's key port of Santos have no plans currently to stage a sympathetic strike later this week in support of workers at the port of Paranagua, the social director of the Administrative Portworkers' Union said.
"At the moment there are no plans to strike, no meetings are scheduled," Wellington de Souza Costa said.
Port operators at Paranagua this afternoon failed to reach agreement with dockworkers over a pay dispute, with a 72-hour strike now scheduled to begin at 1200 local/1500 GMT Wednesday.
Monday, there had been some suggestion that should the Paranagua strike go ahead, other ports would hold sympathy stoppages as of Thursday.
General dissatisfaction over the privatisation of the country's ports has meant Santos has been on strike alert for some time, Costa said.
"There is concern about working conditions, job stability, people don't sleep well at night," Costa said.
"But that is one thing and the Paranagua situation is another," he said.
Directors from the National Portworkers' Federation were unavailable to comment on the possibility of more nation-wide stoppages.

Paranagua is the country's key soybeans and soyproducts port. Earlier today the port authority played down the possible impact of any strike as it said loading is carried out by conveyor belts, meaning that a few people were needed to operate the terminal.
